findings: Adversarial review of 0.2.5 in three rounds, every attack run against real git in scratch copies (bare remote plus clones). Round one found two blocking defects (clean -f left the squash's debris in new folders so the checkout back to the slice failed; settling by keeping the slice's side made save say nothing to save and left the update stuck) and two material ones (a Markdown underline read as a mark; status counted a settled, un-added file as unsettled). Round two found the first fix's per-file parent check let real marks into history and made update abort with an empty GIT error on a conflict in such a file or in a binary file. The third commit fixes all of it: GIT versus conflict decided from the unmerged entries, a per-line parent check, binary and one-sided conflicts named in update, status and the next step, save checks the tree before staging anything, one view for status, save and update. Verified on the final build: setext underline on main with a conflict elsewhere settles and saves with two parents and the underline kept; a conflict in a file whose parents hold the underline is refused MARKERS_LEFT while the marks are in and stages nothing on refusal (both files stay UU), then saves clean; keep-ours saves one merge with MERGE_HEAD gone; modify/delete named, keep or delete then save; a real binary conflict (NUL bytes) named as binary, the chosen copy saved; the failed squash with a file in a new folder and a missing blob leaves main clean and the folder on the slice; a plain save with nothing changed still says nothing to save. npm test 26 pass, npm run lines 1062, no em dash in the diff, 0.2.5 in package.json, package-lock.json and src/mcp.js, every backlog row true against the diff, README and CLAUDE.md sentences true. Left as polish, no code change: status keeps listing a binary conflict as to settle until the save, since the tool cannot tell a chosen copy from the one git left; the MCP test's actor argument is dropped by the zod schema and never read by the handlers, which the test proves by outcome.
